sections.h2: How Cabarrus County values and bills a house
sections.html:
Every parcel in Cabarrus is appraised at market value as of January 1. The owner then receives a single bill that adds the county rate to whatever city, town and fire district rates cover the address. Current values date from January 1, 2024, and no flat percentage was applied to earlier assessments.

Three pieces make up a parcel's value: the land, the building (its type, age and physical traits) and extras like garages, sheds, pools, fences and driveways. A structure still going up is valued by how complete it is on January 1, and that figure goes into the bill.

State law, G.S. 105-286, allows at most eight years between reappraisals. Cabarrus cut that gap in half so values follow the market more closely.

sections.h2: Who to contact about assessments and appeals
sections.html:
The Tax Administration department handles assessment and appeals, and the Revaluation office answers value questions at 704-920-2126 or revalinfo@cabarruscounty.us. The office is at 65 Church Street S in Concord, NC 28025, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

Collections handles billing for every jurisdiction in the county: the county itself, seven cities or towns and 16 fire districts. Appeals go to the Equalization and Review Board, whose members are residents with local real estate knowledge, appointed by the County Commissioners.

  • Real estate values and property cards: the county's online real estate search, by name, address or parcel
  • Comparable sales: a map-based comparable sales tool on the Tax Revaluation page
  • Relief programs: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker, plus present use value and wildlife conservation programs
  • Payment plans: the Collections office

sections.h2: How to appeal your Cabarrus County value
sections.html:
Ask for an informal review in writing. No particular form is needed, though more evidence makes a stronger case. The appraiser covering your area reviews what you send and replies with an Informal Review notice that also explains how to move to the formal level.

Once that notice arrives, you have 30 days to keep the appeal going. To ask for a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review, write to Cabarrus County Tax Revaluation, PO Box 707, Concord, NC 28026-0707, or file through the county's online system. The assessor's office must receive it within 30 days of the date printed on your Notice of Real Estate Assessed Value, or at any point before the Board adjourns. Adjournment usually comes in late April, and the local newspaper carries the date.

Once you submit, you and the county appraiser get one more look at the case, and you fill out an Application for Hearing. The board listens to both sides, and its decision letter follows by mail within a month of the hearing. If you still disagree, the next stop is the NC Property Tax Commission. G.S. 105-290 requires a written notice of appeal with your grounds, filed 30 days or less after the ruling was mailed.

A big jump between two revaluations is not a valid ground for appeal. Compare your parcel with similar sales instead.

The due date is September 1, and a bill turns delinquent if it is unpaid after January 5 of the next year. Mailing happens once a year, in late July or the first days of August, for real estate, business and personal property alike.

Cabarrus County tax calendar
WhenWhat happens

Interest under G.S. 105-360 is 2 percent from January 6 to February 1, followed by three-fourths of one percent for each month after. A delinquent bill can lead to collection actions or tax foreclosure. Collections can set up a payment plan, but you must request it, preferably early in the year, and the full bill is still owed by the delinquent date.

The county rate for 2026 is $0.576 per $100 of assessed value, and each city or town and fire district adds its own rate. Kannapolis, for example, adds $0.5595 on top of the county rate for an address inside the city.

Rates are set during the budget process, with the Board of Commissioners and each municipality finishing theirs no later than June 30. A change in assessed value may or may not change your bill, because the effect is unknown until the rates are set. To estimate your own bill, use the county's real estate search for the assessed value and the rate page for each district that covers your parcel, then ask Collections to confirm.

sections.h2: Tax breaks for Cabarrus County homeowners
sections.html:
Cabarrus has three relief programs on the county's list: homestead, disabled veteran and circuit breaker. You pick only one, and the application form, AV-9, goes to the county assessor by June 1 ahead of the tax year. Present use value for farm, forest and wildlife land is handled separately with its own applications.

  • Homestead (G.S. 105-277.1): open to an owner at least 65, or totally and permanently disabled, whose income is below $38,800 for 2026. The county leaves out $25,000 of value or half the appraisal, whichever is more.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value drops out of the bill. The state form sets no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: after five years in the home, your tax is held to 4.0% of income, or to 5.0% if income lands above the cap but no higher than $58,200 for 2026. Savings are deferred and secured by a lien.

sections.h2: Who pays the bill when you sell
sections.html:
Plan to pay the current year's bill from the sale proceeds, as G.S. 105-355. The county issues the bill to whoever owned the parcel on January 1, so if you sold during the year, hand the bill to the buyer.

Median value for an owner-occupied home here is $354,800, and 71.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. The real estate search shows values set as of January 1, 2024, so look at recent neighborhood sales before you list. Your closing attorney should get a payoff for all taxes due, fire district amounts included. Collections can tell you whether any earlier year is delinquent.

Pull your property card from the real estate search and check the land, building and extras the county has on file. Look at the comparable sales tool to see how nearby homes sold. Ask Collections for the current year's balance and any prior-year delinquency. If you receive homestead or circuit breaker relief, tell your closing attorney, since a deferral can come due. Last, confirm which bill goes to the buyer after closing, because the county issues it to whoever owned the parcel on January 1.

faqs.q: When are Cabarrus County property taxes due?
faqs.a: September 1. A bill is past due if not paid before the following January 5, and state law starts interest on January 6. Bills are mailed in late July or the first days of August.

faqs.q: How often does Cabarrus County revalue real estate?
faqs.a: Every four years by local choice, although state law only requires every eight. The current values are as of January 1, 2024. The Revaluation office at 704-920-2126 can confirm the next cycle.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cabarrus County property value?
faqs.a: Submit a written request for an informal review, then appeal to the Board of Equalization and Review within 30 days of your value notice or before the board adjourns, usually in late April. The decision letter arrives within 30 days of the hearing.

faqs.q: Does Cabarrus County allow installments on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Collections office works with taxpayers on payment plans, but you must request one and the bill still has to be paid in full by the delinquent date. Contacting them early in the year is preferred.

faqs.q: Who gets the bill if my Cabarrus County house sells before year end?
faqs.a: The bill still goes out in the name of the owner on January 1, so forward it to the buyer if you receive it after closing. Settle the current year's tax through closing so it does not turn into a lien problem for the new owner.
